title: Python: starOverride refuses two stars that bind the same symbol when the holder has a def or import of the name (lost edge, GCLI-127 round 1)
description: Found measuring GCLI-127 round 1 (opum-ai/glyph-cli#204). A LOST edge, not a wrong one. starOverride (src/python/calls.ts, landed by GCLI-125) refuses a may-skip deciding star whenever an earlier star after the last unconditional binding exports the name, without checking that the earlier star binds a DIFFERENT symbol. Input: b.py def f; m.py is 'def f():' then 'from b import *' then 'if C:' with 'from b import *' inside; app 'from m import f; f()' (and 'import m; m.f()'). Python binds b.f either way, so one edge is correct; dev gives no edge (star-bound) in both forms. Same for 'from b import f' + 'from b import *' + 'if C: from b import *', and for 'def f' + 'from y import *' + 'if C: from b import *' with y.py 'from b import f'. Fix shape: the check GCLI-127 now applies in resolveStarAttribute: refuse only when the earlier star is incomplete or resolveStarBound of the earlier target gives anything other than the same single symbol the deciding star gives. Not on the hold list: a lost edge, soundness holds.

acceptanceCriteria.text: the three inputs give b.f in both forms, red before and green after with callees pinned and the full bin delta
an earlier star that binds a DIFFERENT symbol, or is incomplete, still refuses
a mutant that restores refuse-whenever-the-earlier-star-exports is observed red
the five-pin corpus diff against dev is script-asserted with every moved site named; any in-repo edge created or removed comes to opum-doc before the clear
